newsitem.title: UK: American agrees in principle with Stagecoach.
newsitem.headline: American agrees in principle with Stagecoach.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines, the U.S. transatlantic carrier, said on Tuesday it had an "agreement in principle" with Stagecoach Holdings Plc's South West Trains after earlier filing a writ over the rail company's use of the "Advantage" name.
An American Airlines spokeswoman refused to comment further on the matter.
Sources said American filed a writ against Stagecoach Holdings Plc's South West Trains over the rail company's use of the "Advantage" name in some of its brochures.
American Airlines uses "Advantage" as the name for its frequent flyer programme.
Earlier, a spokeswoman for SW Trains said it was aware of the writ and added that the two parties had "reached an agreement in principle. But it is not finalised."
